what_happened: Found agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/adoption-lint-conventions.md, a pre-existing binding design doc governing lint scope/convention decisions (allowlist vs zero-tolerance decision rule, dual-mode root resolution requirement), and determined this task's lint is a different class than the doc's 'adoption lint' requirement (2) (executable-surface-only scope) since the dispatch's own named sites are mostly context/ and docs/ files. This resolved the lint's scope/convention design cleanly without needing a new ad hoc rule.

Research report had already independently re-verified every measured figure (188 lines/92 files, 46 valid commands, 23 existing gates, command-output.md's four sub-class B sites) and read both NET-SIZE candidate hosts in full source, so this plan dispatch needed only four confirmatory greps before writing phases -- no re-exploration.

git-commit-phase.sh's (and git-commit-scoped.sh's) Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check never contains a file_scope entry ending in /** against any path, including its own direct children: the case pattern "$entry"/* quotes the glob metacharacters in $entry so they are matched LITERALLY, not as a wildcard. This drops agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json and agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json from this task's phase-3 commit even though agent-system/extensions/core/** is declared in file_scope and plainly intended to cover them (the plan's own author worked around the same bug by listing two OTHER core/scripts/* files as exact entries). Left both files uncommitted in the working tree pending a safe way to extend file_scope (update-task-status.sh --file-scope-add is restricted to operation=postflight with target_status in {research,plan}, not usable mid-implement) or a fix to the predicate itself (likely task 394's territory). Reported as a non-blocking issue; proceeding with implementation.
